newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: OUTLOOK - Malaysian palm oil output rise at low rate.
newsitem.headline: OUTLOOK - Malaysian palm oil output rise at low rate.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil production is unlikely to maintain its growth in 1997 because of labour shortages and lower yields, an official of the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) said in a report.

"Malaysian palm oil production is expected to increase at a lower rate in 1997. The problem of labour shortage and low oil extraction rate are expected to check on the increase in production," said the report by Mamat Bin Salleh released in Dhaka on Monday as part of Malaysian-sponsored Palm Oil Week.
Malaysia's palm oil production is expected to reach 8.9 million tonnes this year, up 6.1 percent from 1996, which itself was up 7.4 percent from 1995.
After meeting domestic consumption of 1.3 million tonnes in the year and allowing for some inventory, only about 7.6 million tonnes would be available for export this year, it said.
Exports totalled 7.197 million tonnes in 1996, the report said. Malayasia earned $4.5 billion through exports of palm oil in 1996.

Mohammad Yusof Hashim, the chief executive of Malayasian Palm Oil Promotion Council, said on Monday that world palm oil production would rise to about 29 million tonnes by the year 2010, of which Malaysia would account for 11 million tonnes.
World palm oil production totalled 16 million tonnes in 1996 or 16.7 percent of the world's oils and fat production of 96 million tonnes.

Hashim said world oils and fat consumption was expected to reach 105 million tonnes by the year 2000 and 130 million tonnes by 2010, "with a growth of population, economy and per capita consumptioon."
He said there had been attempts to discredit palm oil on "quite unjustified health grounds."

"The truth has prevailed and palm oil has overcome all odds to emerge as number one oil in the international oils and fats trade," he told the ceremony marking Palm Oil Week in Dhaka organised by the council.
Hasim said: "Malaysian palm oil is indeed unique as it is the only vegetable oil with a balanced composition of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids."
He said the area under oil palm in Malaysia was expanded to 850,000 hectares in 1978, to 1.3 million hectares in 1983 and 2.6 million in 1996.
Pakistan is the largest buyer of Malaysian palm oil followed by India, China and West Asia, he said but gave no details.
Hashim said Bangladesh's imports of crude palm olein rose to 103,000 tonnes in 1996 from only 15,000 tonnes in 1995.

"This development was not only because of a more favourable price situation in 1996, but also as a result of a reduction of import duty by the government (Bangladesh) on crude palm olein from 45 percent to 30 percent," he said.

He also felt that Bangladesh should reduce import duty further to increase the consumption of oils and fats in the country, which is one of the lowest at 4.5 kilogram per person annually against a global average of about 15 kg.
Bangladesh imports nearly 370,000 tonnes of oil and fats a year at a cost of about $200 million.
